newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 7.5/8.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 7.5/8.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 7.5/8.0 percent on Friday on ample supply, dealers said.
They said ample supply was sustained following central bank injection of some 1.284 trillion rupiah into the market.
Swap rates also fell across the board on ample supply, driving longer-term rates in the money market to follow.
One Japanese bank dealer said one-month money was already offered at 13.0 percent and three-month money at 14.0 percent.
Dealers said weekly tax payments due Friday were small and may start building up again in the second week.
One local bank dealer said operators were seen selling long-dated swaps and covered through short dates which helped limit further declines of short-dated swap rates.
Overnight swaps were at 0.25/0.35 points and tom/next at 0.10/0.17. Overnight swaps were traded below par last week.
The local bank dealer said this might indicate the forming of bottom line which could soon spread over to longer-term swaps when operators start covering long dates.

The central bank offered 3-4 day bilateral SBIs at seven percent, 5-6 day at 10.0 percent, seven day at 10.5 percent, 10-12 day at 11.0 percent, 13-17 day at 11.25 percent, 18-24 day at 11.50 percent, one-month at 12.0 percent, three-month at 13.0 percent, six- at 13.25 and 12-month at 13.50 percent.
Bond dealers said the market was still thin and they would start quoting again next week. The benchmark PLN V/A bond was yielding 16.14 percent at the end of last year.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 8.5 percent, compared with 8.25 percent on Monday.
